articles.title: Find a banknote with a ‘solid’ serial number? It’s probably worth so much more
articles.summary: Banknotes with "solid" serial numbers have routinely sold for thousands on auction sites — if they're in excellent condition.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Building a collection of unique banknotes? You'd be off to a solid start if you find one with a "solid" serial number.

A "solid" serial number, as known to collectors, is a serial number on a U.S. banknote that features only a single repeating digit, such as "11111111" or "77777777." Bills with such numbers might not be quite as rare as, say, a discontinued banknote or a bill with a double denomination error, but they're still among some of the most recognized "oddities" in paper-money collecting, according to Doug Mudd, the curator and director of the American Numismatics Association's Edward C. Rochette Money Museum in Colorado.

"As a type, they are somewhat popular because they are more readily noticeable," Mudd tells Nexstar.

Mudd pointed out, however, that a "solid" serial number is technically "just as rare or common as any other," mathematically speaking. But much like collectors who seek out "radar" serial numbers (i.e., palindromic numbers, such as 12344321 or 55433455), there are indeed niche collectors willing to pay well over face value for more unique specimens.

In fact, banknotes with solid serial numbers generally fetch more than other so-called "fancy" serial numbers, seeing as there are fewer possible bills with solid numbers in a series.

"Many collectors don't have a solid among their fancy serial number notes," one member of Reddit's r/PaperMoney community remarked in a post about a collector who found a "solid" $20 banknote earlier this year.

"Right place, right time, I guess," the user said.

Archived auction data from Heritage Auctions and Stacks Bowers shows that solid-numbered bills have routinely sold for thousands of dollars apiece, if they're in good condition. Some buyers have also paid premiums for specific solid numbers like 77777777 or 88888888 — numbers thought to be more lucky or auspicious in certain cultures. (A "near-perfect" $100 bill with a solid 8 serial number sold for more than $19,000 in 2024, the Heritage Auction website indicates.)

Imperfect bills with solid serial numbers can still fetch many times their face value, recent eBay sales indicate. An ungraded $1 note with a solid 3 serial number sold for $1,600 earlier this month, while a $5 bill with a solid 2 serial number sold for $2,660 as part of a series with several other bills of sequential serial numbers. The auction platform also appears to be crawling with "near solid" or "almost solid" banknotes for sale (e.g., 44444447 or 91999999), though those were selling for far less.

Mudd, meanwhile, told Nexstar that bills with fancy serial numbers are generally less "interesting" to most paper-money hobbyists or historians, as they aren't exactly anomalies, and don't come with much of a story. But when it comes sheer value, these bills certainly have their buyers.

"[They're] definitely worthwhile to the specialist," Mudd said. "[…] There are people very interested in them and they will pay more money."

articles.title: 8 leaf-peeping destinations that belong on your fall travel list
articles.summary: From Nevada's high-mountain aspens to Kentucky's sandstone gorges, these autumn escapes prove brilliant color isn't limited to New England.
articles.body:
When people talk about fall foliage, certain destinations tend to dominate the conversation. Vermont and New Hampshire have their maple-covered mountains, while Colorado's golden aspens draw leaf peepers into the Rockies each September. The Blue Ridge Parkway and Great Smoky Mountains aren't exactly secrets, either.

But deciduous trees grow in plenty of places that haven't built entire tourism industries or a national reputation around their annual color change. Some of the country's most interesting fall landscapes can be found in the sandstone gorges of Ohio and Kentucky, the lake country of northern Minnesota and even the mountains of Nevada.

The following 8 destinations aren't necessarily undiscovered — locals certainly know what happens when the leaves begin to turn — but they remain surprisingly overlooked on the national fall travel circuit. Better yet, there's plenty to do once you arrive besides stare at trees.

The Ozarks are one of the country's most overlooked regions for fall color. The rugged Boston Mountains of northwestern Arkansas are covered in oak, maple, hickory, sassafras and other hardwoods that turn shades of yellow, orange, red and even a little purple if you look hard enough. Better yet for procrastinating leaf peepers, the show arrives relatively late — color generally begins appearing by the second week of October and peaks in late October, extending into early November.

A great way to explore is behind the wheel. The Pig Trail Scenic Byway twists through heavily forested mountains along Arkansas Highway 23, while the Boston Mountains Scenic Loop crosses the range through deep valleys and high ridges with sweeping views across the Ozarks.

But plan to spend some time outside the car too. Devil's Den State Park has miles of hiking and mountain biking trails through sandstone bluffs, caves and narrow ravines, while Ozark National Forest offers everything from short walks to longer hikes into the backcountry. Farther east, the Buffalo National River flows beneath limestone bluffs through the heart of the Ozarks.

Ohio doesn't have much of a national reputation for dramatic landscapes, which is part of what makes a first visit to Hocking Hills so surprising. About an hour southeast of Columbus, the region is carved into sandstone cliffs, narrow gorges, waterfalls and caves surrounded by thick forest. Unlike much of Ohio, this corner of the state escaped the flattening effects of the Ice Age glaciers. Instead, over millions of years, streams cut through the region's sandstone, creating the rugged landscape visitors see today.

Those formations make the fall color particularly interesting. Trails descend into narrow gorges where hemlocks remain dark green beneath sandstone cliffs; hardwoods, meanwhile, turn crimson overhead. The classic hike follows the gorge from Old Man's Cave toward Cedar Falls , passing beneath rock overhangs and alongside streams and waterfalls. Ash Cave, Conkle's Hollow and Rock House offer more chances to explore the cliffs, recess caves and forested ravines that make Hocking Hills unlike much of the surrounding Midwest.

Fall color typically peaks around the middle of October. Beyond the best-known trails, spend some time exploring the surrounding back roads that lead to Wayne National Forest — check out the Wildcat Hollow Trail , which is particularly good in the fall. Lake Logan offers paddling and fishing beneath the changing trees.

Nevada isn't the first state that comes to mind for leaf-peeping — makes sense, considering much of it is desert terrain. But among the exceptions is Great Basin National Park , where Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive climbs from the desert near the Utah border to more than 10,000 feet above sea level. Sagebrush and pinyon-juniper woodland give way to mountain forest, and near the top of the road, groves of aspens spread across the slopes of the Snake Range. In the fall, they turn yellow, red, and gold.

Explore Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive — which climbs more than 4,000 vertical feet in 12 miles — then hike the Alpine Lakes Loop or take the Bristlecone Trail to a grove of ancient Great Basin bristlecone pines beneath Wheeler Peak, where some trees are thousands of years old. Below ground, ranger-led tours explore the stalactites and stalagmites of Lehman Caves. Stick around after dark too: Great Basin's remote location and exceptionally dark skies make it one of the better places for stargazing .

Aspens generally begin changing around the second or third week of September, with timing varying by elevation and weather. The upper Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive is typically accessible through October, but snow can close it earlier — a reminder that despite the Nevada address, this is very much a high-mountain fall trip.

California has the highest mountains in the Lower 48, but it rarely enters the national leaf-peeping conversation. Why? Some things in life are just strange. Head east of the Sierra Nevada in the fall and you'll be in on the secret.

The town of Bishop makes a good base. Roads climb west from the Owens Valley into Bishop Creek Canyon , where groves of aspen grow around creeks and alpine lakes beneath the steep granite walls of the Sierra Nevada. North Lake, Lake Sabrina and South Lake are among the most reliable stops, with the color gradually working its way down from the high country from late September through late October.

Spend a day hiking or driving Bishop Creek, but leave time for Highway 395 — it showcases mountains rising abruptly from the desert. North of Bishop, the road follows the eastern wall of the Sierra toward Mammoth Lakes, with easy detours into mountain canyons along the way. Stop at Convict Lake for a short hike around the water beneath a wall of steep, exposed peaks, or continue into the Mammoth Lakes Basin for more trails and groves of changing aspen.

Lake Superior's North Shore gets plenty of attention during Minnesota's fall color season, but a lesser-known road heads inland from Grand Marais. The Gunflint Trail runs nearly 60 miles through Superior National Forest toward the Canadian border and the edge of the Boundary Waters, passing rocky ridges and dozens of lakes along the way. This is classic North Woods country, with spruce and pine forests broken up by birch, maple and aspen that light up with color each fall.

Driving the Gunflint is worthwhile, but hiking and paddling are recommended. Canoe one of the many lakes along the route or climb Honeymoon Bluff to a rocky overlook above Hungry Jack Lake and the surrounding forest. Farther up the trail, the Magnetic Rock Trail crosses open bedrock and boreal forest on its way to a large, iron-rich rock with enough magnetism to move a compass needle. For a bigger adventure, the Gunflint also provides several entry points into the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness .

Timing can vary considerably, even over short distances in northern Minnesota, but the Gunflint Trail is often strongest from late September into early October. Because wildfires affected parts of Superior National Forest in 2026, check current closures and conditions before heading into the Boundary Waters.

Most travelers visit the Black Hills in summer, when Mount Rushmore and the region's winding scenic roads are at their busiest. Fall provides a compelling reason to wait. Spearfish Canyon cuts through the northern Black Hills between high limestone walls, with Spearfish Creek running alongside the road and waterfalls tucked into side canyons. Spruce and ponderosa pine keep much of the landscape green while aspens, birches and other deciduous trees change colors.

The canyon is only one piece of the trip. Continue south through the Black Hills to Custer State Park , where the 18-mile Wildlife Loop Road passes through rolling prairie and pine forest inhabited by bison, pronghorn, elk and bighorn sheep. Needles Highway winds through some of the region's granite spires, and hikers can climb Black Elk Peak, the highest point in South Dakota, for views across the surrounding hills.

Color typically peaks from late September into early October, which is also a good time to visit Mount Rushmore. The memorial remains open throughout October, while the enormous summer crowds begin to taper off after Labor Day.

The Pennsylvania Wilds stretch across a huge swath of sparsely populated northern Pennsylvania. Hardwood forest covers much of the region, turning the rolling hills and river valleys red, orange and gold in early October. It's a big landscape by eastern standards, with enough public land to string together several days of hiking, scenic drives and wildlife watching.

Allegheny National Forest is a great place to start. The 36-mile Longhouse National Scenic Byway loops through oak, black cherry and hemlock forest around the Allegheny Reservoir, with stops at Rimrock and Jakes Rocks for views across the water and surrounding hills. Jakes Rocks also has more than 35 miles of mountain-bike trails, and the reservoir itself opens up another way to see the foliage by kayak or canoe.

Farther east, Kinzua Bridge State Park contains an intriguing landmark: the remains of a massive railroad viaduct, partially destroyed by a tornado in 2003 and repurposed as a pedestrian skywalk. From there, you can look across the Kinzua Creek Valley, where foliage generally peaks during the first two weeks of October. (The skywalk will remain open through Oct. 31, 2026, while a larger rehabilitation project continues.) Fall also overlaps with the elk rut, and the area around Benezette is one of the best places in the Pennsylvania Wilds to see and hear bugling bull elk.

Kentucky has bourbon and horse country pretty well covered from a tourism standpoint, but its fall foliage tends to get less attention. That's a shame in the Red River Gorge, where one of the East's more unusual landscapes sits within Daniel Boone National Forest . Sandstone cliffs and natural arches rise above a heavily wooded network of ravines and ridges. In October, the fall color makes the geology come to life even more.

For a first visit, hike to Gray's Arch or choose one of the trails along Auxier Ridge, where viewpoints look across miles of forest and sandstone formations. Natural Bridge State Resort Park is nearby, and the Red River Gorge Scenic Byway offers an easier way to see the landscape by car.

Color usually reaches its best from mid-to-late October, when cooler temperatures make it an ideal time to spend long days outdoors. And there is plenty left to discover. More than 100 natural sandstone arches are scattered throughout the Red River Gorge Geological Area — go and see as many as you can.

articles.body:

Saiba aqui como ver se o seu nome está na lista de convocados e como proceder para recuperar o celular.

O documento traz a lista completa dos proprietários convocados, além de locais, datas, horários e a documentação necessária para a retirada dos smartphones. CLIQUE AQUI PARA VER.

🗓️ As entregas dos aparelhos serão realizadas nos dias 18, 21 e 22 de setembro, seguindo um cronograma específico por região.

A Polícia Civil ressalta que estar com o nome na lista não garante a entrega automática: o aparelho só será liberado após a conferência e validação da documentação (veja qual a documentação abaixo).

Interior do Estado: A entrega será feita no dia 18 de setembro, nas sedes das 13 Delegacias Regionais do RN (como Caicó, Pau dos Ferros, Macau, Nova Cruz, Patu, Alexandria, Santa Cruz, João Câmara, Currais Novos, Assú e Goianinha). Documento oficial de identificação com foto (original);

Boletim de Ocorrência registrado na época do roubo ou furto (se disponível);

Outras informações que comprovem que o bem lhe pertence.

Caso o titular do aparelho não possa comparecer, é possível indicar um representante legal, que deverá apresentar uma procuração específica com firma reconhecida em cartório, segundo a Polícia Civil.

articles.title: Corpo de Bombeiros em Mongaguá: cidade ganha primeira estação | G1
articles.standfirst: Durante a cerimônia, também foi inaugurada a nova sede da Defesa Civil Municipal.
articles.summary: Com investimento de R$ 1,6 milhão, a primeira estação do Corpo de Bombeiros em Mongaguá agilizará o socorro e reforçará a segurança no litoral.
articles.body:
A cidade de Mongaguá (SP) era único município da região sem uma unidade própria do Corpo de Bombeiros. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Mongaguá

Mongaguá , no litoral de São Paulo, ganhou a primeira estação do Corpo de Bombeiros da cidade. A estrutura recebeu investimento de cerca de R$ 1,65 milhão do Governo de São Paulo. A estação deve reduzir o tempo de resposta em ocorrências, segundo a prefeitura.

A unidade foi instalada por meio de um convênio entre o Estado, através da Secretaria da Segurança Pública (SSP), e a administração municipal. A cidade cedeu o imóvel e realizou as adequações necessárias para o funcionamento da corporação.

Do total investido pelo Estado, R$ 1.285 milhão foi destinado à compra de uma viatura Auto Bomba Salvamento e Resgate (ABSR). O veículo é equipado para atuar em diferentes tipos de emergências. Outros R$ 357 mil foram aplicados na aquisição de equipamentos operacionais, enquanto aproximadamente R$ 15 mil foram destinados a materiais de infraestrutura administrativa.

Segundo o comandante de Bombeiros do Interior 3, coronel PM Alessandro Lima de Freitas, os profissionais destinados à unidade estão entre os mais habilitados e capacitados para atuar nas ocorrências.

"O sonho dos mongaguenses de ter uma unidade do Corpo de Bombeiros aqui foi realizado. É também o nosso sonho, porque as instituições querem estar presentes e atender com mais qualidade, rapidez e eficiência a quem precisa", afirmou o coronel, segundo nota divulgada pela prefeitura.

A expectativa da administração municipal é também que a presença permanente da corporação permita atendimento mais rápido, especialmente em situações nas quais o deslocamento de equipes de outros municípios poderia aumentar o tempo de resposta.

Durante a mesma cerimônia, a prefeitura inaugurou a nova sede da Defesa Civil Municipal, instalada ao lado da estação dos Bombeiros. A proximidade deve facilitar a atuação conjunta em ocorrências como chuvas fortes, ressacas, ventos e alagamentos.

O administração municipal também entregou quatro viaturas. A Guarda Civil Municipal recebeu veículos para a Ronda Maria da Penha e o Grupamento Ambiental, enquanto a Defesa Civil e o Semutran receberam uma viatura cada.

Outro anúncio foi a apresentação da delegada Carolina Brambila Rocha como nova titular da Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Mongaguá.

Durante a cerimônia, foram entregues viaturas para diferentes corporações. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Mongaguá

articles.title: Taxa de analfabetismo cai no Acre e chega a menos de 10%, diz IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Índice era de 9,4% em 2025 e acompanhou queda nacional. Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA) contribuiu para a redução da taxa.
articles.summary: Índice era de 9,4% em 2025 e acompanhou queda nacional. Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA) contribuiu para a redução da taxa.
articles.body:
Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA) contribuiu para a redução da taxa — Foto: Stalin Melo/Secretaria de Educação e Cultura (SEE)

📚 A taxa de analfabetismo entre pessoas de 15 anos ou mais caiu no Acre em 2025 e chegou a 8,9%, segundo dados da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (Pnad Contínua). Em 2024, o índice era de 9,4%.

A redução acompanha uma queda registrada em todo o país. No Brasil, a taxa de analfabetismo chegou a 4,9% em 2025, conforme os números divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

👩‍🏫 É considerado alfabetizado quem sabe ler e escrever um bilhete simples.

Segundo o último levantamento da Pnad, divulgado em junho, dentre os 57 mil acreanos que eram analfabetos no estado, 30 mil eram homens e 27 mil mulheres. O estudo também apontou uma desigualdade racial: 6 mil pessoas brancas contra 49 mil pessoas pretas ou pardas.

Uma das alternativas que explicam a queda no analfabetismo é o Cadastro da Educação de Jovens e Adultos (CadEJA), uma plataforma criada para registrar o interesse de pessoas que desejam voltar a estudar, levando elas para escolas da rede pública de ensino.

A população com 15 anos ou mais está entre o público atendido pelas políticas de Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA). A modalidade é destinada a pessoas que não tiveram a oportunidade de concluir a educação básica na idade considerada regular.

No Acre, 341 escolas públicas e privadas oferecem EJA, contudo, desse total, 334 pertencem à rede pública. Em relação às matrículas, o estado contabiliza 21.041 estudantes na modalidade, considerando as redes pública e privada. Apenas na rede pública, são 20.535 matrículas.

Além disso, na Região Norte, o Acre aparece com o terceiro maior número de matrículas na EJA, atrás apenas do Amazonas, que registrou 54.986, e do Pará, que ficou no topo na região norte, com 119.486 matrículas em 2025.

Para ampliar o acesso à educação de jovens e adultos e combater o analfabetismo, o Ministério da Educação (MEC) desenvolve ações através do Pacto Nacional pela Superação do Analfabetismo e Qualificação da EJA (Pacto EJA).

articles.title: A $100 billion “ghost city” became a home for tech entrepreneurs, but the experiment lasted less than two years after it began
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Forest City was meant to become a futuristic metropolis near Singapore, but its empty towers and quiet streets earned it a very different reputation. .
articles.body: Forest City was meant to become a futuristic metropolis near Singapore, but its empty towers and quiet streets earned it a very different reputation. That unusual setting later attracted a group of technology entrepreneurs who saw the underused development as an opportunity to test a new way of living and working. In 2024, Network School arrived with a community built around technology, startups and the ideas of Balaji Srinivasan’s The Network State. Participants lived, worked and learned together inside the development. Yet the experiment faced practical problems, including living conditions, licensing issues and scrutiny from Malaysian authorities. Less than two years after it began, Network School was ordered to cease operations.How Forest City’s ghost-town reputation helped attract a new technology communityForest City was conceived as an enormous mixed-use development in Johor, close to the Singapore border. The project included high-rise residential buildings, hotels, retail areas and recreational facilities, with plans originally aimed at accommodating hundreds of thousands of people. According to the BBC, around $100 billion has been associated with the development over the years.Large parts of the development remained underoccupied, giving Forest City its reputation as a ghost town. The Covid-19 pandemic made the situation harder, while wider problems affecting China's property sector added to the difficulties facing the project. Streets and apartment blocks existed, but there were not enough people using them to create the ordinary bustle associated with a major urban centre.Srinivasan’s Network State idea became a real-world experiment in Forest CitySrinivasan had been developing his thinking about alternative communities for years before arriving in Forest City.His 2022 book, The Network State, proposed a model in which people could first gather digitally around shared interests and beliefs, build businesses and financial relationships, acquire physical territory and eventually seek some form of political recognition.Srinivasan, a former Coinbase chief technology officer who had also worked in venture capital and co-founded genomics company Counsyl, had spent much of his career around technology and startups. The school was not simply intended as a conventional educational programme. It combined accommodation, work space, classes, fitness and communal activities, giving participants the chance to live together while developing companies and pursuing projects.According to Fortune, the first programme began in Forest City in 2024. Participants reportedly paid about $1,500 a month, with accommodation, food, classes and access to facilities included.Why Forest City attracted technology workersForest City itself was hardly the main attraction for everyone who arrived. The appeal was the possibility of spending months around other people working on technology businesses, investing, engineering or internet-based projects. Instead of travelling between conferences and temporary coworking spaces, residents could live in one place with a ready-made professional network around them.The development had modern buildings and leisure facilities, while its location in Johor put Singapore within relatively easy reach. The surroundings were very different from the crowded technology centres usually associated with startups.For someone working remotely, a half-empty city could be useful. Residents described a routine built around shared meals, exercise, work and classes. The programme also attracted people interested in Srinivasan's broader ideas about technology, community and governance. Reports have described participants arriving from different countries, including digital nomads and young technology workers looking for a concentrated environment in which to build projects.Life inside the Network SchoolSome residents complained about mold in accommodation, something Srinivasan attributed in part to the humid local climate. Others found that Forest City lacked the restaurants, nightlife and variety of activities they might have expected from a major city. There were also complaints about the imbalance between men and women among participants.A group can work well online while remaining relatively loose. Living together exposes different problems. People have to share physical spaces, deal with maintenance and rules, and decide what happens when the surrounding town does not provide everything they want.The Network School could provide its own meals, activities and social environment. Network School did not have to build a city from scratch. It arrived at a place where towers, roads, hotels and amenities had already been constructed.The problem Forest City was facing was almost the reverse. That gave Srinivasan an unusually large experiment space. A community of technology workers could occupy part of an underused development without having to solve the enormous construction costs normally involved in establishing a new urban district.The arrangement also made the project's ambitions easier to observe. The Network School was not an abstract online community. People actually lived together, worked together and tried to form relationships around a shared set of ideas.Inside Forest City’s short-lived tech communityNetwork School remained tiny compared with the scale of Forest City. The development had been conceived for a population in the hundreds of thousands, while the school was dealing with hundreds of participants at most. Its presence therefore did not transform Forest City into a functioning metropolis.For a period, an otherwise underpopulated collection of towers became a meeting point for people interested in startups, cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence, digital communities and alternative forms of organisation. It offered something that conventional technology campuses generally cannot: the chance to live with the professional network rather than commute to it.A community can be highly active internally while remaining almost completely disconnected from the life around it. articles.title: S Korea's revised espionage law: How it affects countries beyond North Korea
articles.summary: Rest of World News: South Korea implemented its expanded espionage law on Sunday, broadening espionage offences beyond acts involving North Korea to include all foreign c.
articles.body: South Korea implemented its expanded espionage law on Sunday, broadening espionage offences beyond acts involving North Korea to include all foreign countries.South Korea’s National Assembly had passed the revised Criminal Act on February 26. The amendment was promulgated on March 12 and comes into effect on Sunday, after a six-month grace period.The move comes after years of criticism that Seoul’s existing laws were ill-suited to punish technology and industrial espionage involving non-North Korean actors, especially China.The revised act carries a minimum sentence of three years in prison for the offence of conducting espionage for a foreign country or equivalent organisation. Existing provisions for espionage benefiting an “enemy state” remain in place.Earlier, prosecutors had to rely on other industrial technology or trade-secret laws, in many cases involving foreign entities.According to Reuters, Seoul’s national intelligence service welcomed the amendment when it was passed, saying it would strengthen South Korea’s ability to prevent leaks of strategic technologies such as semiconductors, displays, batteries and AI.Chinese espionage attemptsThe change follows high-profile technology leak cases, including last year’s indictment of five former Samsung Electronics employees accused of transferring key dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chip technology to Chinese memory maker CXMT.Asked whether the law, which does not specify any country, could be seen as targeting Beijing, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, Mao Ning, said China requires its enterprises to conduct international cooperation in accordance with international rules and laws.“At the same time, to this end, we believe that all countries should safeguard the normal investment and business activities of enterprises and provide a fair, just, and non-discriminatory business environment,” Mao told a regular news briefing on Friday.Earlier, the United States accused Chinese artificial intelligence firms, including DeepSeek and Alibaba, of stealing trade secrets from their American counterparts to cut development costs and swiftly release coveted technologies to the market.According to a joint advisory by USA’s Federal Bureau of Investigation, National Security Agency and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, major Chinese technology firms were found to be extracting “restricted proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US frontier AI models”, using “distillation” techniques, where smaller models are trained on more advanced architectures.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: What to do and what not to do after 'Ganpati Sthapana' and Ganesha's arrival at home
articles.summary: Trending News: There is a certain feeling when Ganpati comes home.The house may be full of people, there may be flowers everywhere, someone is busy making modaks whi.
articles.body: There is a certain feeling when Ganpati comes home.The house may be full of people, there may be flowers everywhere, someone is busy making modaks while another person is still trying to fix the decorations. And then comes the moment everyone has been waiting for - Ganpati Sthapana.Once Lord Ganesha is placed in the home, the celebrations begin. But for families that follow the traditional rituals, there are also a few things to keep in mind during the days Ganpati stays at home.These customs aren't exactly the same in every household. Some families follow elaborate puja rituals, while others keep things simple. The number of days the idol stays at home can also vary.Still, there are some common practices devotees usually follow after Ganpati Sthapana.Keep the space around Ganpati cleanThis is perhaps one of the simplest things to follow.Once the idol has been installed, the area around it should be kept clean. Flowers that have wilted, leftover food, used puja items and other waste shouldn't be allowed to pile up around the idol.And because the puja area tends to become a busy spot during Ganesh Chaturthi, it can get messy rather quickly. A little regular cleaning can make a big difference.Make time for daily pujaGanpati doesn't just arrive for the Sthapana and then become part of the home decor.Traditionally, devotees offer prayers every day while the idol is kept at home. Depending on the family's customs, this could include aarti, flowers, durva, sweets, fruits and other offerings.It doesn't have to be a lengthy ritual every single time. For some families, morning or evening aarti is enough. Others may have a more detailed puja routine.The important thing is to follow the tradition your family normally observes.Don't forget the modaksCan Ganesh Chaturthi really feel complete without modaks?The sweet is closely associated with Lord Ganesha and is commonly offered as prasad during the festival. Homemade modaks are a favourite in many homes, although ladoos, fruits and other vegetarian foods may also be offered.Once the offering has been made, the prasad can be shared with family members and guests.There is no need to turn every day's offering into a huge feast. A simple, fresh offering works perfectly well for families that prefer keeping the celebrations low-key.Be careful with food offeringsFresh food is generally preferred for puja.In Delhi's September heat, for example, milk-based sweets or other perishable foods shouldn't be left sitting outside for hours. Once the puja is over, food that needs refrigeration should be stored properly.And if something has spoiled, don't eat it simply because it was offered during the puja. Prasad should still be safe to consume.Try to keep the atmosphere peacefulGanesh Chaturthi can get loud and lively, especially when relatives and friends start dropping in for darshan.That's part of the fun.But traditionally, the period is also seen as a time for prayer and devotion. So unnecessary arguments, fights or deliberately disruptive behaviour around the puja area are best avoided.Nobody expects a household to suddenly become completely silent for 10 days. Families will talk, children will play and guests will come over. The idea is simply to maintain a respectful atmosphere around Ganpati.Don't move the idol unnecessarilyOnce the Sthapana has been performed, devotees generally avoid moving the idol without a reason.The exact customs can differ, particularly depending on how and where the idol has been installed. So if there is a genuine need to shift it, families may prefer to follow the guidance of their priest or the tradition they have been following for years.This is one area where there isn't necessarily one rule that applies to every home.Follow your family's tradition for VisarjanOne of the biggest questions around Ganpati is often: When should the visarjan happen?There isn't one answer for every household.Some families bring Ganpati home for one and a half days. Others keep the idol for three, five, seven or 10 days. Some families follow different timings altogether.The visarjan day is usually decided according to the family's tradition and, in some cases, the preferred muhurat.So if your neighbour is doing visarjan on a different day, there's no reason to assume your family is doing something wrong.Don't turn the festival into a wasteful celebrationWith flowers, decorations, food and guests, it is easy for the amount of waste at home to go up during Ganesh Chaturthi.There are simple ways around that.Reusable decorations can be used instead of buying new ones every year. Food can be prepared according to the number of people actually expected at home. And flowers and other puja waste can be disposed of responsibly.Many families also choose eco-friendly Ganpati idols, particularly because of concerns around the impact of immersion on water bodies.What about non-vegetarian food?This is another area where customs can differ.Many families follow a vegetarian diet during the period Ganpati is at home, while others may have their own established practices. Some households avoid certain foods only on the main puja days.There is no need to assume that every family follows exactly the same food rules. If your household has a particular tradition, that's the one to follow.Don't get too stressed about getting every ritual perfectThis may be the most useful thing to remember.Ganesh Chaturthi comes with plenty of rituals, and if you're celebrating at home for the first time, it can sometimes feel like there is a long list of things you're supposed to remember.But traditions aren't identical across India. A Maharashtrian household may have different customs from a family in Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka or Bengal. Even two families from the same city may celebrate differently.If you're unsure about a particular ritual, check with your family priest or an elder who knows your family's tradition rather than relying on random rules circulating online.At its heart, Ganesh Chaturthi is about welcoming Lord Ganesha into the home with devotion and joy.So keep the puja space clean, offer fresh food and prayers, treat the idol with respect and follow the customs your family believes in.And yes, make those modaks. Ganpati would probably expect nothing less.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: A Tanzanian biologist fed bacteria discarded fruit and vegetables to replace fishmeal; the resulting feed reportedly brought fish to market 40% sooner and raised farmers’ profits 25%
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how Diana Orembe, a Tanzanian biologist, is transforming fish farming by creating sustainable feed from discarded fruits and vegetables, resulting in faster growth and increased profits for farmers.
articles.body: In much of East Africa, small-scale fish farming seems easy enough on paper, but it keeps hitting the same wall: the cost of feeding the fish. In Tanzania, feed alone can account for around seventy percent of the expenditures of running a small farm, and much of that feed relies on either imported soybean or fishmeal manufactured from wild-caught fish, both of which come with hefty price tags and environmental impacts of their own. But for Diana Orembe, a biologist working in Dar es Salaam, the imbalance seemed less like an inevitable aspect of the industry and more like a problem waiting for the proper kind of microbe.Orembe co-founded the biotech firm NovFeed before being selected by UNICEF Innovation as one of its young innovators addressing climate-related challenges. The basic material is leftover fruit and vegetables collected from schools, universities and local markets across the city, garbage that would otherwise simply rot. UNICEF Innovation included Orembe in its cohort of young innovators addressing climate-related challenges. Her company, NovFeed, uses bacterial fermentation to convert discarded vegetables into a protein ingredient for fish feed.Making fish food out of garbageThe procedure involves adding a special blend of bacteria to the collected waste, and the microbes consume the material, reassembling its nutrients into a concentrated protein for farmed fish. Dar es Salaam produces thousands of tonnes of waste every day, a lot of it organic; thus, the raw material for this process is almost endless and almost free, an entirely different starting point than buying soybean meal from the other side of the planet. The resulting feed also floats instead of sinking, which can reduce feed losses when conventional pellets settle on the pond floor before fish consume them.NovFeed’s process starts with organic waste collected mainly from schools, universities and markets in Dar es Salaam. The company separates useful organic material before fermentation, allowing its microbes to act as a biological factory that converts the waste into single-cell protein for fish feed. UNICEF says the main ingredients are agri-waste and bacterial cells, and that the resulting protein can replace traditional fishmeal and soybean. The process also avoids dependence on wild-caught fish as a protein source and turns organic waste into an input for aquaculture rather than leaving it to decompose. NovFeed was established in 2020, and the company has continued developing the technology with an emphasis on scaling the protein for fish-feed production.More growth, more profitsThe actual outcomes have been measured directly on farms and not merely in a laboratory. Fish that were fed the fermented feed reached market weight about forty per cent faster than fish fed conventional feed, and farmers that used the fermented feed reported a twenty-five per cent increase in their total profits. The approach also reduces reliance on fishmeal made from wild-caught fish, easing pressure on marine fish stocks that would otherwise be used as feed.Recognition beyond the farm gateThe wider food and sustainability world has taken notice too. The project was later highlighted by the Food Planet Prize, while NovFeed went on to win a $1-million Milken-Motsepe Prize in AgriTech. What began as a solution to a single country’s feed issue has become a demonstration of something larger: that the garbage sitting in a market bin may be worth more to a fish farmer than the imported alternatives propping up the sector. The bacteria did the heavy job, but it needed a biologist prepared to see decaying fruit as an opportunity, not an issue, to make the notion work.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how UNICEF's WASH Houses are revolutionizing sanitation and hygiene for nomadic schoolchildren in Mongolia, providing heated toilets and warm water to ensure their well-being even in extreme winter conditions.
articles.body: For children in Mongolia’s remote herding communities, using a toilet could mean leaving a heated classroom and stepping outside into temperatures far below freezing. Many rural schools and kindergartens depended on outdoor latrines, while access to warm water for washing was limited. The problem was especially difficult in a country where nomadic families move with their livestock and frozen ground can complicate conventional construction.According to UNICEF, the organisation developed relocatable WASH Houses in Mongolia by adapting the principles of insulated shipping-container construction. The units provided toilets and basins with warm running water in heated, well-lit structures that could be connected to classrooms or ger kindergartens. By 2015, 15 WASH Houses had been installed alongside ger kindergartens and regular classrooms, directly benefiting about 1,400 students.Building a bathroom that could survive winterThe WASH House was developed as a prefabricated and relocatable solution for Mongolia's harsh climate. The organisation worked with local partners to develop several models based on insulated shipping-container structures. Rather than building every facility from scratch at the school site, the units could be manufactured elsewhere and transported to remote communities. The design addressed one of the biggest problems facing sanitation infrastructure in Mongolia: freezing temperatures. The units were insulated and heated, while their water and sanitation systems were designed to operate in winter conditions. They contained toilets and washing facilities supplied with warm water, giving children access to basic hygiene without having to leave the building for an outdoor latrine.The facility’s portability was especially useful for ger schools and kindergartens. A ger is a round tent-like home traditionally used by Mongolian herding families, and schools in remote areas often have to adapt to that way of life. A portable sanitation facility can offer more flexibility compared to a regular building made of bricks and concrete. UNICEF said the units could be adapted to different water and sanitation setups depending on the site. Some could use wells and septic tanks, while others could connect to existing systems.Warm water became part of school lifeIt was not just about making toilets available to them. Water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities affect whether students can access washrooms, maintain personal hygiene, and use toilets safely during the day. UNICEF research on WASH and menstrual health also noted that rural students in Mongolia faced special challenges because sanitation facilities were inadequate and water and separate washing rooms were limited.Research published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health also examined hygiene conditions among Mongolian schoolchildren. A survey of 1,507 fifth-grade pupils in Ulaanbaatar found that access to water and soap at school handwashing facilities was far from universal, showing how infrastructure availability can shape everyday hygiene practices. For the children using the new WASH Houses, the difference was tangible. UNICEF described facilities that allowed pupils to wash with warm water and use toilets inside a heated structure instead of relying on exposed outdoor facilities. The organisation reported that the teachers linked the better WASH conditions with the lack of health-related issues and absenteeism, but this information was not a part of the scientifically controlled evaluation of the WASH Houses. These units solved multiple problems by improving sanitation, reducing children’s exposure to extreme winter weather, and making handwashing easier.A shipping container becomes school infrastructureThe project reflected a broader trend toward designing infrastructure for places where conventional construction is costly or impractical. Mongolia has a short construction season, harsh winters, and long distances between settlements. As a result, it can be difficult to transport materials and build facilities in remote locations. A prefabricated container offered another option, since much of the work could be completed before delivery and the facility could then be connected to local water and sanitation services.The approach did not aim to turn shipping containers into an alternative to regular schools but rather showed that the infrastructure could be adapted to suit the location. An insulated, heated, and mobile bathroom could be built where it was needed without erecting a whole new permanent structure. In remote Mongolian schools, it became a way to provide toilets, hot water, and basic hygiene facilities for children who previously had to endure harsh conditions to meet basic needs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell built his wife a bottle house for her doll collection; about 25,000 glass bottles and 1,750 hours later, it became a roadside attraction
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell and his wife Myrtle built a house from glass bottles in Redditt, a small community in northwestern Ontario, Can.
articles.body: In 1973, Ontario teacher Hank Deverell and his wife Myrtle built a house from glass bottles in Redditt, a small community in northwestern Ontario, Canada. Myrtle wanted a house to display her growing doll collection, and Hank turned the idea into a bottle-built structure that later became a local tourist attraction.The Redditt Bottle House is located along Highway 658, about 20 minutes north of Kenora. The property was created in the early 1970s and includes the bottle house along with other glass and fantasy-themed structures. The unusual construction has since drawn visitors to the area.According to the Kenora Great War Project, Myrtle was previously married to Orley Edgar Neuert, a former Canadian soldier who served with the 13th Battalion during the First World War. Orley and Myrtle had four children and later lived in Redditt, where Orley worked for the Canadian National Railway as a storekeeper and baggageman.Orley died in 1964. Myrtle later married Hank Deverell, who worked as a teacher at Beaver Brae High School in Kenora. The couple lived in Redditt, and in 1973 they built the bottle house to give Myrtle a place to display her doll collection.The structure was made using thousands of glass bottles held together with mortar. About 25,000 bottles and 1,000 pounds of mortar were used to build the attraction. The Deverells also spent about 1,750 hours on the construction.The bottles became the main feature of the property. Village Life described the house as a structure that uses glass to create patterns of colour and light.The property was not limited to the main house. It also came to include a glass windmill and a structure known as the “House of the Three Bears”. These were designed in the same fantasy style as the bottle house.The bottle house did not remain only a personal project for Myrtle and Hank. It soon began attracting visitors. Village Life reported that about 1,500 people visited when the Bottle House first opened in the summer of 1973. Visitors have since travelled from different parts of Canada and other countries to see the glass structures. The attraction also became part of Redditt’s local identity.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 10 countries with the highest forest cover in the world; check India’s rank
articles.summary: For travellers who love greens and dream of disappearing into dense rainforests, walking beneath towering trees or spotting wildlife far from crowded .
articles.body: For travellers who love greens and dream of disappearing into dense rainforests, walking beneath towering trees or spotting wildlife far from crowded tourist trails, some countries offer a very different kind of holiday experience. The Worldometer ranking, based on FAOSTAT data, puts Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States, China, DR Congo, Australia, Indonesia, Peru and India among the top 10 countries by total forest area.Let’s take a deeper look at these countries forest side:Russia (814.8 million hectares)Russia has by far the world's largest forest area, with 814,848,460 hectares of forest. Much of this forest belt forms part of the taiga, the vast boreal forest stretching across Siberia. It is a landscape of conifers, lakes, rivers and long winters. These forests are also natural home to wildlife including brown bears, wolves, lynx and the Siberian tiger. For travellers, Russia's forests offer experiences ranging from remote Siberian wilderness to the forests surrounding Lake Baikal.Brazil (491.57 million hectares)Brazil comes second with 491,570,000 hectares of forest. The country's forest story is dominated by the Amazon, the world's largest tropical rainforest. Travellers visiting Brazil can experience the rainforest around destinations such as Manaus, where river journeys offer access to the Amazon's extraordinary ecosystem.Canada (346.98 million hectares)The third spot is taken by Canada with 346,975,800 hectares of forest. Its forests stretch across huge parts of the country, creating some of the world's most dramatic wilderness landscapes. For travellers, Canada's forests are closely connected with hiking, camping, canoeing and wildlife watching. Bears, moose, wolves and other wildlife can be encountered across different regions.United States (310.65 million hectares)The United States has 310,645,000 hectares of forest, making it the fourth-largest country by total forest area. Travellers can explore the giant trees of California and the Pacific Northwest to the Appalachian forests in the east and the boreal landscapes of Alaska.China (211.41 million hectares)China ranks fifth with 211,405,700 hectares of forest. The country's forests range from subtropical landscapes in the south to temperate and mountainous forests farther north.The bamboo forests around Chengdu and Sichuan offer encounters with giant pandas, while mountainous forest landscapes can be found around destinations such as Zhangjiajie.Democratic Republic of the Congo (151.96 million hectares)The sixth spot is taken by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It has 151,955,200 hectares of forest. Much of this forest forms part of the Congo Basin, one of the world's most important tropical rainforest regions. For adventurous travellers, the country's forests offer rare wildlife experiences. The DRC is home to mountain gorillas, eastern lowland gorillas, chimpanzees and the endangered bonobo.Australia (125.37 million hectares)Australia ranks seventh on the list with 125,367,000 hectares of forest. Its forests look very different and are eucalyptus dominated. Travellers can explore forests around Queensland's Daintree Rainforest, one of Australia's best-known tropical forest destinations, or experience the country's vast eucalyptus landscapes.Indonesia (89.64 million hectares)Indonesia ranks eighth with 89,641,200 hectares of forest. For travellers, some of the most memorable forest experiences can be found on islands such as Sumatra, Borneo and Papua. Sumatra's forests, for instance, are among the places where visitors can seek out orangutans in their natural habitat.Peru (73.64 million hectares)Peru is on the ninth spot on the list with 73,637,800 hectares of forest globally. While Peru is internationally famous for Machu Picchu and the Andes, a huge part of its natural landscape lies in the Amazon Basin. Destinations such as Tambopata and the Amazon around Iquitos offer travellers a very different side of Peru.India (71.04 million hectares)India rounds off the top 10 with 71,038,800 hectares of forest. Travellers can find Himalayan forests in the north, tropical forests in the Western Ghats and Northeast, dry deciduous forests across central India and mangrove ecosystems along the coast. Some of the country's most popular wildlife destinations are forest-based, including Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Corbett, Kaziranga and Ranthambore.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Iran-linked groups used Claude to target US Navy, run propaganda: Report
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iranian state-aligned and Iran-linked groups used Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform to run propaganda campaigns, conduct domestic su.
articles.body: Iranian state-aligned and Iran-linked groups used Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence platform to run propaganda campaigns, conduct domestic surveillance and develop targeting recommendations against US naval forces, according to a threat report released by the company.Anthropic said it disrupted malicious activity involving Claude between December 2025 and August 2026, covering cyber operations, influence campaigns and surveillance. The company said several Iranian-linked accounts had used the AI model to automate or support activities ranging from producing state propaganda to analysing social media users and gathering information on US military positions.The findings come amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States, including attacks involving US and Iranian forces around the Strait of Hormuz. Commercial shipping through the waterway has remained limited as the conflict has continued, with Iran seeking greater control over traffic passing through the strategic strait.Claude used to build Iranian propaganda campaignsAnthropic said it identified and removed three accounts aligned with Iranian state propaganda institutions. The accounts were linked to the Islamic Culture and Communications Organization under Iran’s Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, the Islamic Propaganda Office of Khorasan Razavi and the Islamic Propaganda Organization’s Bina Cultural Observatory.According to Anthropic, the accounts used Claude to develop campaign plans, propaganda doctrine manuals, personas and target databases. They also converted official government intelligence bulletins into tailored content in Farsi, Arabic, Urdu, Malay, Spanish and English, with plans for distribution in as many as 20 languages.The material was spread across X, Instagram, Telegram, TikTok and YouTube, as well as Iranian platforms including Eitaa, Bale and Rubika. Anthropic said some of the content appeared on channels sympathetic to Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) narratives.The company assessed the influence operation as Category Three on its Breakout Scale, indicating that the activity involved distribution across multiple platforms.During the 2026 US-Israel-Iran war, Anthropic said the network also attributed false claims to Western research organisations, including CSIS, Brookings and RAND, in an apparent attempt to make Iranian state-backed narratives appear more credible.Iran-linked account developed US naval targeting toolsAnthropic separately identified an Iran-linked account that used Claude to collect and analyse publicly available information about US naval forces in the region.The account used the AI model to compile targeting handbooks and identify and track naval positions using open-source information, according to the company. Anthropic said the activity involved developing recommendations that could potentially be used against US naval forces.The threat report also detailed the use of Claude by Iranian paramilitary and security-linked units for domestic surveillance. Anthropic said it banned 16 accounts operated by two linked units associated with Iranian paramilitary and security agencies.One organisation claimed to have surveilled and profiled 6,388 Iranians in a single year and maintained an identity database. Anthropic said Claude was used to help build what it assessed was likely a government-controlled surveillance case-management system and to analyse 155,216 tweets.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Might makes right’ logic should have been discarded long ago: Xi at Brics Summit
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Chinese president Xi Jinping on Sunday called on Global South countries to jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs and stre.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chinese president Xi Jinping on Sunday called on Global South countries to jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs and strengthen cooperation across areas including artificial intelligence, trade, digital industries, manufacturing and science and technology.His remarks came at the second session of the 18th Brics Summit, where he also said China would continue opening its economy and sharing the opportunities of its development with other countries.Addressing the summit, Xi said international rules must be written by all countries and rejected the logic of “might makes right”. He called for the principles of sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and peaceful settlement of disputes to be upheld, with international law and rules applied to all without double standards."Fairness and justice is a universal aspiration, and international rules must be written by all countries. The logic of “might makes right” does not hold, and should have been discarded long ago. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards," Xi said.Xi also urged Global South countries to remain committed to a people-centred development philosophy and work towards the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. He said that since China launched the Global Development Initiative five years ago, it had implemented more than 2,000 projects in partnership with other countries and provided training to more than 200,000 professionals, benefiting people in more than 120 countries.He added China had granted zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations and would continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up."China is opening its door ever wider to the world. We have granted zero-tariff treatment for all the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China. We will continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up, and share the opportunities of China’s development with other countries," the Chinese president said.Five initiatives for Brics cooperationXi proposed five initiatives to strengthen BRICS cooperation, focusing on artificial intelligence, trade and investment, digital industries, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development.Under the open source and inclusive AI initiative, China will work to establish a Brics AI open source community, support cooperation in developing and applying large language models, organise specialised AI seminars and training courses, and build an open AI ecosystem.On trade and investment facilitation, Xi proposed a BRICS special economic zone partnership through which countries could establish an intelligent portal, coordinate policies and build a new frontier for open development. He also said China would host the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year.The digital industry cooperation initiative envisages a Brics digital ecosystem cloud platform, along with digital skills training, technological exchanges and industrial alignment.Under the intelligent manufacturing initiative, China offered to assist fellow Brics countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms to promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading.Xi also proposed a Brics engineer cultivation alliance for the joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a Brics youth exchange programme focused on scientific and technological innovation.‘Greater Brics’ push gains momentumXi also unveiled initiatives spanning areas from AI to trade to deepen cooperation among the “Greater Brics” emerging economies, as Beijing seeks to strengthen the grouping as a practical platform for Global South development.Political and security cooperation, along with economic and financial cooperation, remain the grouping’s main focus areas, with India as the 2026 chair and China set to take over in 2027 as the two countries seek wider partnerships to boost Brics’ global clout.The success of the "Greater Brics Initiative" depends on laying a solid foundation for pragmatic cooperation, Xi told the leaders' ​annual summit in New Delhi, the official Xinhua news agency said.'Greater Brics' nations should further co-operate, maintain ⁠the stability of industrial and supply chains, and cultivate an integrated market, Xi told the summit's closing session, as cited by Reuters.Brics has expanded from its original membership of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa to include Iran, Indonesia, Egypt, Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates.It also has 10 partner countries spanning emerging economies across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East, further broadening its reach across the Global South.China and Russia sometimes refer to the expanded bloc as "Greater Brics".PM Modi-Xi meeting focuses on ties and border peaceOn the sidelines of the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Xi held a 40-minute meeting during which they agreed that India and China should take a strategic and long-term view of their relationship and ensure that differences do not turn into disputes.Xi said the current momentum in bilateral ties, built on the resumption of institutional exchanges, an expanding cooperation agenda and growing trade, had been hard-won and should be cherished.PM Modi welcomed the “steady progress” in bilateral relations but underlined that peace and tranquillity in the border areas would remain an essential basis for the continued development of ties.The meeting was the leaders’ third bilateral interaction in two years, following their meetings in Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. It was also their first meeting on Indian soil in seven years.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mayawati on Sunday escalated her criticism of her nephew Akash Anand, saying he continues to act under the influence of his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, days after Anand was 'fully relieved' from the party. The Bahujan Samaj Party chief also accused expelled leaders of attempting to create confusion among BSP workers by spreading rumours about her health.The remarks came after Mayawati removed Akash as the party’s national coordinator on September 3 and subsequently announced that he had been relieved from the BSP. On Saturday, she ruled out political roles for Akash and his brother Ishan Anand, describing the move as her “final decision”.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Mayawati said she had learnt of an alleged phone call made by Akash to Alok Kumar, a party in-charge at her residence, in which he enquired about her health.“It seems that people who have been expelled from the party have been spreading confusion among party members for the past 1-2 days that Behen Ji (Mayawati) is quite ill,” she said.Mayawati said Akash asked Kumar, “whether Behen Ji is ill? How is her health?” According to her, Kumar responded, “No, no, she is absolutely fine and busy with her work.”Also Read| First Akash, then Ishan, now Deepika: A new twist in Mayawati's succession story takes another turnShe further claimed that Akash then told Kumar, “Do not tell Behen Ji that I asked about this,” before ending the call.Mayawati said the episode raised concerns over Akash's independence and linked it to his relationship with Siddharth.“This is also a matter of great concern and seriousness; meaning, in this matter, his mindset might be right or wrong, because even now he is not working with his own mind, but rather seems to be working under the influence of Shri Ashok Siddharth's mind,” she said.Siddharth, Akash's father-in-law, had announced his complete retirement from politics and social life. Mayawati had said the decision was correct but came after a delay despite her ultimatum linking his political retirement to Akash's future in the BSP.She had earlier accused Akash of giving greater importance to “personal and family interests” than the Bahujan movement.On Saturday, in a long post on X, Mayawati said neither Akash nor Ishan would receive any political position in the BSP. She said her brother Anand Kumar could seek assistance from his daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand, who is studying law.Siddharth, Anand’s father-in-law, was expelled from the BSP in March 2025 over allegations of “factionalism”.
